title: Artinian test categories, marked deformations and formal objects
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative Noetherian ring and $k$ a field of finite type over $R$ [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], [def-weil-field], [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. All rings are commutative and all ring maps preserve the unit. A local ring has exactly one maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_A$; an Artinian ring has the descending chain condition on ideals. A map $f:A\to B$ between local rings is local if $f^{-1}(\mathfrak m_B)=\mathfrak m_A$. Define $\mathcal C_{R,k}$ to have objects Artinian local $R$-algebras $A$ with specified $R$-isomorphism $A/\mathfrak m_A\cong k$, and morphisms local $R$-maps inducing the identity on $k$. A small extension $B\twoheadrightarrow A$ is a surjective morphism whose kernel is a one-dimensional $k$-vector space annihilated by $\mathfrak m_B$. A groupoid is a category whose every arrow is invertible. In a chosen transport presentation, a category cofibred in groupoids on $\mathcal C_{R,k}$ is a collection of groupoids $\mathcal F(A)$ with covariant transport functors $f_*:\mathcal F(A)\to\mathcal F(B)$ for morphisms $f:A\to B$ of $\mathcal C_{R,k}$, with natural isomorphisms $e_A:(\mathrm{id}_A)_*\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathrm{Id}$ and $c_{g,f}:g_*f_*\xrightarrow{\sim}(gf)_*$. The two composites from $h_*g_*f_*$ to $(hgf)_*$ agree, and $c_{f,\mathrm{id}}=f_*e_A$, $c_{\mathrm{id},f}=e_Bf_*$ after the identity identifications; these are the unit and associativity axioms of a groupoid-valued pseudofunctor. A predeformation category additionally has $\mathcal F(k)$ equivalent to the groupoid with one object and one arrow. It satisfies (RS) if, for $A_1\to A\leftarrow A_2$ with $A_2\to A$ surjective, the natural functor $\mathcal F(A_1\times_A A_2)\to\mathcal F(A_1)\times_{\mathcal F(A)}\mathcal F(A_2)$ is an equivalence (fully faithful and essentially surjective). Here $A_1\times_A A_2=\{(a_1,a_2):f_1(a_1)=f_2(a_2)\}$ with componentwise operations. The groupoid on the right has triples $(u_1,u_2,\alpha:(u_1)|_A\cong(u_2)|_A)$ as objects and pairs of arrows respecting $\alpha$ as morphisms. Write $\overline{\mathcal F}(A)$ for the set of isomorphism classes in $\mathcal F(A)$. For a finite-dimensional $k$-vector space $V$ [def-weil-finite-dimensional-subspace], let $k[V]=k\oplus V$ with $(a,v)(b,w)=(ab,aw+bv)$ and $R$-structure through $k$ [def-sc-trivial-square-zero-extension]; write $k[\epsilon]=k[k]$. For a predeformation category put $T\mathcal F=\overline{\mathcal F}(k[\epsilon])$. For a complete Noetherian local $R$-algebra $C$ with a specified $R$-isomorphism $C/\mathfrak m_C\cong k$, a formal object $\xi$ is a system $\xi_n\in\mathcal F(C/\mathfrak m_C^n)$ for integers $n\geq1$, together with specified transition isomorphisms $(q_{n+1,n})_*\xi_{n+1}\xrightarrow{\sim}\xi_n$, where $q_{n+1,n}$ is the quotient map. Their composites give the transition isomorphisms for all $m\geq n$, using the composition constraints of $\mathcal F$. A morphism of formal objects over $C$ is a family of arrows at all levels commuting with these transition isomorphisms; completeness means that the canonical map $C\to\varprojlim_n C/\mathfrak m_C^n$ is an isomorphism [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. For a local residue-preserving $R$-map $a:C\to A$ with $A\in\mathcal C_{R,k}$, choose $N$ to be the least positive integer with $\mathfrak m_A^N=0$, which exists by [lem-weil-pbc-artinian-local-noetherian-nilpotent]. Define $\xi_A=(\bar a_N)_*\xi_N$, where $\bar a_N:C/\mathfrak m_C^N\to A$ is induced by $a$; it exists since $a(\mathfrak m_C^N)\subseteq\mathfrak m_A^N=0$. Evaluation from a higher level is identified with this value by the transition isomorphisms and $c_{\bar a_N,q_{m,N}}$; restrictions of evaluations use these same comparisons. A formal object is versal when, for every surjection $B\twoheadrightarrow A$ in the test category, every local $a:C\to A$ inducing the identity on $k$, every $y\in\mathcal F(B)$ and every specified isomorphism $y|_A\cong\xi_A$, there exist a local lift $b:C\to B$ and an isomorphism $y\cong\xi_B$ extending the specified one.
